sections.name: Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.

items.text: Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.
What is a quality of earnings report?

An independent analysis of what a business actually earns, as distinct from what it reports. A CPA firm traces revenue and expenses to bank records and tax filings, identifies the non-recurring, nonoperating and personal items, and produces a normalized earnings figure a buyer or lender can underwrite. It is a consulting engagement under the AICPA’s standards, not an audit, a review or a compilation, and it carries no opinion on the financial statements. The full note.
Is the Pre-Market Assessment a quality of earnings report?

No. It is the first read: an indicative valuation range, your adjusted earnings as you report them, the adjustments a buyer is most likely to question, and a 90-day plan. The preparation review is the full trace, non-attest. The Sell-Side QoE is the report, from the independent CPA firm we partner with. You can stop after any step.
Why have a report on my own company?

Because the buyer will commission one either way, and the price moves on what it finds. In a study published January 27, 2026, of seventy-five signed letters of intent that collapsed in 2025, 21.3 percent ended because the earnings were not what was presented, double the share of two years earlier, and 25.3 percent on a finding outside the earnings work. GF Data’s record of 360 private equity transactions since the third quarter of 2024 shows sellers with a sell-side report averaging 7.4 times adjusted earnings against 7.0 without; that is a correlation, concentrated in larger deals, and we do not read it as a promise. The surer effect is time: diligence proceeds on your record instead of the buyer’s reconstruction of it.
Why does a lender require a third-party report? Could software do it?

From October 1, 2026, an SBA 7(a) acquisition loan at a purchase price of $3 million or more requires a quality of earnings report with a cash proof, performed by an independent financial professional for the lender; a report prepared by or for the seller does not count. The rule is about independence and responsibility, not technology. Software is used inside the work, for mapping, schedules and reconciliations. It cannot hold a license, carry professional liability, or be independent of the parties, and the AICPA’s position is that responsibility for the work product rests with the CPA. The facts, with sources.
Why not take the first offer?

Because the first number is rarely the last. In 841 acquisitions of S&P 1500 companies from 2005 to 2019, the winning bidder’s first bid averaged a 28.6 percent premium and the final price 38.2 percent; only 8 percent of winners won with a single bid. In the lower middle market, 87 percent of deals above $5 million drew three or more offers in the second quarter of 2026. An unsolicited offer arrives before you know what the alternatives would have been. The full note.
Why go through an intermediary rather than deal with a buyer directly?

Deals the seller starts, or takes unsolicited, price lower: target-initiated deals carry lower premiums and lower multiples of earnings, and the gap widens the less the buyer can confirm. Private sellers who hire an advisor receive higher valuations after correcting for who hires one. And buyers say so themselves: in their own words, the attraction of an off-market deal is that there is less competition and the price is attractive. The party who sees the whole market sets the price.
How does a competitive process benefit me?

Not by the count of bidders. The research finds target returns comparable between auctions and negotiations, and final premiums similar regardless of the number of bids. What a process run from your side changes is that the buyer who knows a competing bid is possible prices against it from the first round, and that the terms behind the headline, cash at closing, working capital, earnout and seller note, are set with alternatives in hand. In the lower middle market sellers received 83 to 92 percent of the price in cash at closing in the second quarter of 2026, and across deals with an earnout about 21 cents of each dollar of maximum earnout was paid.
We will not promise that. It shows what your numbers support, and gives you the chance to fix what they do not, before a buyer prices it.
You. Nothing reaches a buyer, an advisor or anyone else without your written permission.
What do you need from me?
To start, a conversation. The review itself begins with an agreed information request under a signed NDA. Patient records and protected health information are never requested.
A sell-side quality of earnings engagement runs four to eight weeks of fieldwork, and the practitioners who do the work recommend commissioning it three to six months before going to market.
